about:
Golden MFG operates as a custom screen printing and embroidery shop in Las Vegas, Nevada. The company provides design, printing, and embroidery services for apparel, banners, flags, and promotional items. No founding year or ownership details are disclosed.

The shop offers bulk screen printing on t-shirts with a 36-piece minimum, alongside on-demand printing for smaller runs. Embroidery services cover caps, polo shirts, and uniform clothing starting at 12 pieces. Custom banners, pop-up banners, and flags are produced in various sizes and finishes rated for outdoor use. An in-house design team prepares digital proofs for client approval before any payment is required. Standard turnaround is 10 business days, with rush options available when capacity allows.

Golden MFG serves businesses needing branded uniforms, promotional merchandise, storefront signage, and marketing materials. Clients range from companies outfitting staff to organizations creating customer-facing merch and event displays.

The company emphasizes personalized service, competitive pricing, and on-time delivery. Its differentiators include a digital sample-and-quote process before commitment, rapid turnaround for small orders, and a focus on adapting artwork to each project’s specific needs.

name: Golden West Telecommunications
old_description: Golden West Telecommunications has been connecting South Dakota people and communities since 1916.
about:
Golden West Telecommunications, a member-owned cooperative, has been headquartered in Wall, South Dakota since its founding in 1916. It began as the first company to stretch telephone lines across the remote plains of western South Dakota.

The cooperative provides fiber-optic internet, voice telephone, and cable television services to residential and business customers across the state. Its business division offers co-managed IT services, unified communications, and dedicated internet and phone solutions. The network spans from the western border to the eastern edge of South Dakota.

Golden West serves households, farms, and enterprises throughout South Dakota. Its customer base includes family-run hospitality operations such as hunting lodges and agricultural producers like beekeepers, alongside small businesses and rural communities.

Organized as a cooperative, Golden West returns surplus earnings to members as capital credits and gives members a voice in governance. The company emphasizes community giving through scholarships, economic development awards, and donations, aiming to keep South Dakota life rewarding.

name: Gomen Furniture Manufacturing Inc
old_description: We carry a wide variety of furniture to meet your needs and budget.
about:
Gomen Furniture Manufacturing Inc. operates from Lynwood, California, where it was founded in 1990 by Leonardo Gonzalez. The company remains family owned and operated, with Gonzalez serving as CEO and his relatives holding key roles — Lily Gonzalez in accounting and Gustavo as production manager. The business began with a vision to become one of California's top furniture manufacturers, a goal reflected in its continued focus on domestic production.

The company manufactures a full range of living room furniture, including sofas, love seats, sectionals, chaises, and beds under the Gomen and Leotoni labels. A showroom in Lynwood allows buyers to review materials and work with in-house designers on custom configurations. The firm cites 5,000 customers and 1,950 design concepts developed since inception.

Primary customers are furniture retailers and store owners across the Los Angeles region and beyond; testimonials on the site come from store owners praising design flexibility and turnaround. The product line spans transitional and contemporary styles suited for both residential and office settings, with customization offered on dimensions, reclining mechanisms, and fabric choices.

Gonzalez frames the company's purpose around turning a client's stylistic vision into a furnished reality, emphasizing made-in-the-USA construction, affordable pricing, and a hands-on design service that differentiates the operation from import-driven competitors.

name: Good Shepherd Woodshop
old_description: Handcrafted Custom Cutting Boards, Butcher Blocks & Charcuterie Boards made in the USA
about:
Good Shepherd Woodshop is based in Allen, Texas, where founder and head craftsman Joseph Timineri, together with co-founder and wife Crystal Timineri, launched a family-owned operation dedicated to heirloom-quality cutting boards. Crystal manages orders and customer relationships while contributing design direction, and the shop has grown into a local favorite known for its attention to detail and personal touch.

The workshop produces custom cutting boards, butcher blocks, charcuterie boards, and epoxy resin serving boards, all handcrafted from sustainable hardwoods and epoxy resin. Each board is one-of-a-kind, with wood pieces thoughtfully arranged to highlight natural grain patterns and finished for lasting durability. The work remains small-batch, with every item made to order in the shop.

Customers include professional chefs, avid grillers, and passionate home cooks who use the boards as both kitchen tools and serving platters. The product line also targets the gift market for weddings, housewarmings, and holidays. A portion of proceeds is donated to animal rescue organizations, aligning with the founders’ values.

The company was founded to honor the timeless art of woodworking and deliver pieces that are as functional as they are beautiful, grounded in integrity, artistry, and service.

about:
Good Start Packaging operates from Bedford, New Hampshire, supplying compostable food-service packaging to businesses across the contiguous United States. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The firm stocks a broad range of disposable containers, utensils, cups, bowls, bags, and straws sourced from brands such as World Centric, Good Natured, Vegware, Greenware, BioBag, Duro Bag, and its own Good Start Packaging line. It also offers custom printing on select items and operates a "Find a Composter" directory to help customers locate composting services.

Customers include independent cafés, restaurants, bakeries, farms, and wellness-focused retailers — examples shown on the site include an organic food shop, a waterfront café, a wellness brand, a family farmstead, and a bakery. The wholesale model targets food-service operators seeking plant-based, PFAS-free alternatives to traditional plastic packaging.

Good Start Packaging positions itself as mission-driven, emphasizing American-made products and a commitment to sustainability. The "We Make It Our Business to Do Good" tagline reflects a stated goal of reducing plastic waste while providing functional, certified compostable options.

name: Gould Metal Works Co
old_description: Family owned and operated since 1988.  We are at 20 West 19th Street in Covington, Kentucky.
about:
Gould Metal Works Co has operated from Covington, Kentucky since its founding in 1988. The family-owned and operated business is located at 20 West 19th Street.

The shop provides fabrication and installation of structural and miscellaneous steel products, including stairs, handrails, platforms, catwalks, mezzanines, and ladders with or without cages. It also works sheet and plate metal of all gauges in carbon steel, aluminum, stainless steel, and galvanized steel, offering rolling, forming, punching, shearing, and cutting. Additional output includes duct work, drip pans, tables, cabinets, tool boxes, and custom made-to-order items. Tank fabrication covers vessels up to 100,000 gallons with coned, flat, or dish bottoms and hoppers. The company also handles wrought iron railings, gates, fences, and walk-in welding jobs. In-house equipment supports shearing and forming from 18 gauge to 1/2 inch at 10-foot widths, rolling to 1/2 inch at 6-foot widths, plasma cutting, punching, notching, angle cutting, and all types of welding.

The company serves clients needing custom structural steel, architectural metalwork, industrial tanks, and sheet metal components. Its customer base includes construction, industrial, and commercial projects that require fabricated and installed steel assemblies.

Gould Metal Works emphasizes custom design based on customer requirements and a commitment to analyzing needs to recommend designs that meet project schedules.

name: Graff Electric
old_description: For top-notch commercial electrician services in Wolsey, SD, turn to Graff Electric. experienced and reliable professionals serving Wolsey and surrounding areas with exceptional electrical solutions.
about:
Graff Electric is based in Wolsey, South Dakota, and was founded by Jaylon Graff to provide electrical services across central South Dakota. The company is locally owned and operated, with Graff personally overseeing every job.

The firm handles residential, commercial, and farm electrical work, including repairs, panel and service upgrades (100- to 200-amp), wiring and rewiring, lighting and fixture installation, outlet and switch installation, circuit breaker work, meter and meter-base service, and storm-damage response. The crew consists of Graff and technician Sam, operating from a single location in Wolsey.

Customers include homeowners in Beadle and Hand counties, agricultural operations needing farmstead wiring, grain-site circuits, and service-drop repair, as well as commercial properties throughout the region. The service area covers Wolsey, Huron, Highmore, Miller, Redfield, Doland, Wessington Springs, and surrounding communities.

Graff Electric differentiates itself through an owner-operated model that ensures the person who quotes the job performs the work, free on-site estimates, per-job pricing rather than hourly rates, same-day storm response when conditions allow, and a practice of cleaning each job site and following up with the customer.

name: Grand Hawaii Electric LLC
about:
Grand Hawaii Electric LLC operates from Honolulu, Hawaii. Founder Johny Le, a licensed C‑13 electrical contractor, started the company after a decade crews on major O‘ahu projects — among them the Waikīkī International Market Place redevelopment, the Ae‘o and Whole Foods Ward high‑rise, the HART rail stations, and military work at Fort Shafter and the DISA Project. Le’s background includes a carpentry degree from Honolulu Community College (2008‑2010) and apprenticeship through IBEW 1186 and Associated Builders and Contractors.

The firm provides electrical repairs, troubleshooting, panel replacements, outlet and switch upgrades, LED lighting installations, EV charger installations, and general electrical contracting for residential and light‑commercial customers. It does not take on new‑construction work, focusing on service, maintenance, and retrofit projects across O‘ahu. Precision tools such as Leica Geosystem layout machines are used for complex installations.

Clients include homeowners, property managers, and small businesses such as Airbnb hosts, as well as commercial accounts needing code‑compliant upgrades. The founder’s project history also references high‑rise residential towers (A‘ali‘i, Central Ala Moana, Sky Ala Moana), healthcare (Tripler Hospital), and transit (HART Rail), though current operations center on service calls and upgrades.

Le says the business was built on upfront pricing, fast communication, and clean, safe workmanship — standards carried over from large‑project experience. Grand Hawaii Electric now offers a franchise program to replicate its service model and operational systems for other electricians.
